meta.titre: Mutagens and Mutations: what changes DNA, what follows and how to reduce exposure
meta.sous_theme: Mutations, mutagenic agents and their effects

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In the X-ray room of a hospital the radiographer steps behind a protective screen or wears a lead apron, and every woman is asked whether she may be pregnant before a scan. A smoker, a farmer who sunbathes all day in the fields, and a worker near radioactive material all have something in common: their cells are exposed to agents that can change DNA. GCE questions ask you to define a mutation, name the agents that cause it and describe what a mutation can do to a person and to the next generation.

items: DNA is found in the chromosomes in the nucleus, and a gene is a section of DNA that carries the instructions for making one protein.
A human body cell has 46 chromosomes and a human gamete (sperm or egg) has 23.
Body cells divide by mitosis, and gametes are made by meiosis.
Characters are inherited because genes pass from parents to children in the gametes.

sections.titre: Mutations and the agents that cause them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What a mutation is

A **mutation** is a sudden change in the genetic material: either in the structure of a gene (a **gene mutation**) or in the structure or number of chromosomes (a **chromosome mutation**). A **mutagen** (mutagenic agent) is anything that increases the rate of mutation. Mutations also occur naturally and rarely, when DNA is copied with a mistake.

### Mutagens

| Group | Examples |
|---|---|
| Ionising radiation | X-rays, gamma rays, radiation from radioactive substances |
| Ultraviolet radiation | Ultraviolet light in strong sunlight |
| Chemicals | Mustard gas, tar and other substances in tobacco smoke |

### Effects of mutations

Most mutations are harmful, many have no effect, and a very few are useful and add to the variation on which natural selection acts.

- **Mutation in a body cell**: it may be passed to the cells formed from it, and it can make cells divide without control, causing cancer, for example skin cancer after too much ultraviolet light. It is not passed to children.
- **Mutation in a gamete or in the cells of an embryo**: it can be inherited, and may cause a genetic disorder. High doses of radiation to a pregnant woman can damage the embryo and cause deformities or abortion (miscarriage).

### Examples

- Sickle-cell anaemia: a gene mutation that causes abnormal haemoglobin.
- Albinism: a gene mutation, usually recessive, that prevents normal production of melanin.
- Down syndrome: a chromosome mutation in which a person has 47 chromosomes, with an extra chromosome 21. It can arise when chromosomes fail to separate during the formation of gametes.

variantes.nom: Gene mutation compared with chromosome mutation
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks you to classify a named disorder.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A gene mutation changes one gene, so the chromosome number is normal (sickle-cell anaemia, albinism). A chromosome mutation changes the number of chromosomes or breaks or loses part of a chromosome (Down syndrome, with 47 chromosomes).

variantes.nom: Body-cell mutation compared with gamete mutation
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks whether a mutation can be inherited.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Only a mutation in a gamete, or in the cells that make gametes, can be passed to the next generation. A mutation in a skin or liver cell stays in that person and the cells that descend from it; its main danger is cancer.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks how people can reduce their risk.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Radiographers use lead aprons and screens and keep exposure time short; X-rays are used on a pregnant woman only when essential; people avoid long exposure to strong sunlight and avoid smoking; workers handle harmful chemicals with protective clothing.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain why a mutation in the sex cells is more important for the next generation than a mutation in the skin cells, and name one disorder caused by a gene mutation. *(5 marks)*

etapes.justification: The command word is explain, and two kinds of cell must be compared.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Compare sex cells (gametes) with skin (body) cells in terms of inheritance.

etapes.justification: The effect of a body-cell mutation is limited to the person.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A mutation in a skin cell stays in that cell and the cells that descend from it, may lead to cancer, and is **not inherited**.

etapes.justification: The mutated gamete takes part in fertilisation.
etapes.resultat_markdown: If a mutated gamete forms a zygote, the mutation is present in **every cell** of the child and can be passed on again.

etapes.justification: A named example earns the last mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: **Sickle-cell anaemia** is caused by a gene mutation that produces abnormal haemoglobin.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** A mutation in a skin cell affects only that cell and its descendants and may cause cancer, but it is not passed to children. A mutation in a sex cell can be inherited: if the gamete is involved in fertilisation, the mutation is found in every cell of the child and can be passed to later generations. An example of a disorder caused by a gene mutation is sickle-cell anaemia.

items.erreur_markdown: "A mutation is any change in an organism, such as a cut on the skin."
items.pourquoi_faux: A mutation is a change in the genetic material (a gene or chromosomes), not an injury.
items.correction_markdown: A mutation is a sudden change in a gene or in the chromosomes.

items.pourquoi_faux: Many mutations have no effect, and a few are useful. For example, people who carry one allele for sickle-cell anaemia are better protected against severe malaria.
items.correction_markdown: Most mutations are harmful, but some are neutral and a few are advantageous.

items.erreur_markdown: "X-rays only do harm to the body."
items.pourquoi_faux: X-rays are very useful in medicine, for example to show broken bones. They are mutagenic, so the dose must be limited.
items.correction_markdown: X-rays are useful for diagnosis but are harmful in large or repeated doses.

items.erreur_markdown: "Sunlight causes a mutation in a skin cell, so the person's children will inherit it."
items.pourquoi_faux: Only mutations in gametes, or in cells that form gametes, can be inherited.
items.correction_markdown: A body-cell mutation is not inherited, but it can cause cancer.

items.erreur_markdown: "A person with Down syndrome has 45 chromosomes."
items.pourquoi_faux: There is an extra chromosome, not a missing one.
items.correction_markdown: A person with Down syndrome has **47** chromosomes in each body cell.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) What is a mutagen? (b) Name two types of radiation that are mutagenic. (c) Name one chemical mutagen. (d) State one possible effect of a mutation in a body cell.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A mutagen is an agent that increases the rate of mutation. (b) **X-rays** and **ultraviolet light** (gamma rays are also correct). (c) **Mustard gas** or tar in tobacco smoke. (d) It can make the cell divide out of control and cause **cancer**.

items.enonce_markdown: Say whether each change is a gene mutation or a chromosome mutation. (i) A person has 47 chromosomes in every body cell. (ii) A child makes abnormal haemoglobin because of a change in one gene. (iii) A child cannot make melanin because of a change in one gene. (iv) A piece of a chromosome is lost. Then explain why a mutation in one skin cell of a father cannot be passed to his children.
items.solution_markdown: (i) **Chromosome mutation**. (ii) **Gene mutation**. (iii) **Gene mutation**. (iv) **Chromosome mutation**. Children develop from a zygote formed by the father's sperm and the mother's egg. A mutation in a skin cell is not in the sperm, so it cannot be passed to the children.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) An egg containing 24 chromosomes is fertilised by a normal sperm. How many chromosomes are in the zygote and in each body cell of the child? (b) Two parents are both carriers of the recessive allele for albinism ($Aa$). Draw the Punnett square and find the probability that a child is albino. (c) In a group of 1\,200 children of such carrier couples, how many albino children are expected, on average?
items.solution_markdown: (a) A normal sperm has 23 chromosomes, so $24 + 23 = 47$: **47 chromosomes** in the zygote and in every body cell of the child. (b) The gametes are $A$ or $a$ from each parent, giving the genotypes $AA$, $Aa$, $aA$ and $aa$. Only $aa$ is albino, so the probability is $\frac{1}{4}$, that is **25 %**. (c) $\frac{1}{4} \times 1\,200 = 300$, so about **300 albino children** are expected.

items_markdown: A mutation is a sudden change in a gene (gene mutation) or in the chromosomes (chromosome mutation).
Mutagens include X-rays, gamma rays, ultraviolet light, mustard gas and substances in tobacco smoke.
Mutations in body cells can cause cancer but are not inherited; mutations in gametes can be inherited.
Most mutations are harmful, some are neutral and a few are useful.
Examples: sickle-cell anaemia and albinism (gene mutations), Down syndrome (47 chromosomes).
Protection: lead aprons and screens, limited X-ray doses in pregnancy, less exposure to strong sunlight, no smoking.
